subject: biology
title: Metabolism
key_idea: Metabolism is the sum of all the reactions in a cell or the body. The energy from respiration drives enzyme-controlled reactions that build large molecules from small ones. Other reactions break large molecules down into their small units.

blocks.text: Every reaction in your cells is part of your metabolism. Respiration supplies the energy for the reactions that build new molecules.

items.meaning: The sum of all the reactions in a cell or the body.
Building a larger molecule from smaller ones.
A small unit that joins with others to make a larger molecule.
A large molecule made of many monomers joined together.

items: The energy transferred by respiration is used for continual, enzyme-controlled reactions that synthesise new molecules.
Respiration is itself part of metabolism.
Breaking down excess proteins to make urea for excretion is also part of metabolism.

items.text: Glycerol and fatty acids to a lipid
Lipid to glycerol and fatty acids

items: Metabolism is all the reactions in a cell or the body.
Its reactions are controlled by enzymes and use energy from respiration.
Some reactions build molecules up and others break them down.

blocks.text: Cells join small molecules together to make the large molecules they need.

rows: Starch is stored in plant cells and glycogen in animal cells. Cellulose strengthens plant cell walls.
One glycerol molecule joins to three fatty acid molecules.
Plants make amino acids from glucose and nitrate ions.

items: Glucose is joined to make starch, glycogen and cellulose.
A lipid is made from 1 glycerol and 3 fatty acids.
Glucose and nitrate ions make amino acids, which are used to synthesise proteins.

blocks.text: Enzymes also break large molecules into their small units. The small units can then be absorbed into cells.

items: Starch is broken down to glucose by amylase, a carbohydrase. The starch fits the active site and the bonds between glucose molecules are broken.
Proteins are broken down to amino acids by protease enzymes.
Lipids are broken down by lipase to fatty acids and glycerol. The fatty acids are acidic, so the pH falls.
Glucose, amino acids, fatty acids and glycerol move into cells from the blood.
Excess amino acids are broken down to form urea, which is excreted.
Polymers are broken down into monomers by enzymes.
Lipase breaks lipids into fatty acids and glycerol, and the fatty acids lower the pH.
Urea is made from the breakdown of excess proteins.

blocks.text: Metabolic rate is how fast the reactions of metabolism go. It is higher when the body is more active, because more respiration releases more energy.

items: A swimming fish has a higher metabolic rate than a resting fish, because movement needs more energy and so more respiration.
The mean metabolic rate of humans falls with age, for example from 53 to 36 kJ/m²/hour in males between 5 and 45 years old.

blocks.label: Percentage decrease
where: original and new values in the same unit, for example kJ/m²/hour

diagram.alt: Practise calculating a percentage decrease in mean metabolic rate.
diagram.question: The mean metabolic rate of a group fell from **{a} kJ/m²/hour** to **{b} kJ/m²/hour**. Calculate the percentage decrease. Give your answer to 1 decimal place.

items: More activity means more respiration, so a higher metabolic rate.
Always divide the decrease by the original value.

checks.a: The sum of all the reactions in a cell or the body.

checks.q: Describe how nitrate ions are used in a plant to help it grow.
checks.a: Nitrate ions are used with glucose to form amino acids. The amino acids are used to synthesise proteins needed for growth.

checks.q: Which molecules are joined to make a lipid?
checks.a: One molecule of glycerol and three molecules of fatty acids.

worked_example.question:
Nitrate ions are essential for plants to grow.

Describe how nitrate ions are used in a plant to help the plant grow.
answer_points: Nitrate ions are used with glucose.
The amino acids are used to synthesise proteins (needed for growth).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each step in the chain: nitrate ions and glucose, then amino acids, then proteins.

worked_example.question:
5 cm³ of milk B and 1 cm³ of lipase were added to a test tube. The pH of this mixture was pH 7.

This test tube was placed in a water bath for 10 minutes. The pH of the mixture changed from pH 7 to pH 5.

Explain what caused this change in pH.
answer_points: Lipase digests (breaks down) fat or lipid.
Which are acidic, lowering the pH of the mixture (allow: removing fat makes the milk more acidic).
worked_example.tip: One mark for each link: lipase digests fat, fatty acids are formed, and the fatty acids are acidic.

worked_example.question:
The cell wall in the plant cell is made from a carbohydrate called cellulose. Cellulose is a polymer.

Explain why sugars are needed to make the cell wall.
answer_points: Sugars are joined together to make the polymer (cellulose).
Allow: cellulose is made up of sugar or glucose monomers, for 2 marks.
worked_example.tip: Use the words monomer and polymer. Glucose is accepted as the sugar.

worked_example.question:
Enzymes are proteins.

State the names of the chemical elements found in all proteins.
worked_example.tip: Carbohydrates and fats have carbon, hydrogen and oxygen. Only proteins also have nitrogen.

blocks.text: This section lists the chemical elements in the three main food molecules.

rows: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. Some also contain sulfur.

items: Nitrogen is the element found in proteins but not in carbohydrates or fats.
Enzymes are proteins. They are biological catalysts that speed up all the reactions of metabolism.

worked_example.question:
Plants convert the glucose they produce into starch.

Explain why plants store carbohydrate as starch rather than as glucose.
answer_points: So it does not have an osmotic effect on the plant cell, and does not diffuse out of the cells.
worked_example.tip: Glucose is soluble, so it would draw water into the cell and could diffuse out.

blocks.text: This section lists the chemical elements in the three main food molecules.

rows: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen. Some also contain sulfur.

items: Starch and glycogen are made from simple sugars.
Starch is **insoluble**, so it is a good store: it does not affect the water balance of the cell.
